newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dry spell to persist in France for next five days.
newsitem.headline: Dry spell to persist in France for next five days.

text.p: French weather forecasters on Friday predicted another five days without rain across most of the country's farm districts.
Patrick Galois, forecaster with national weather service Meteo France, saw no rain on the horizon in northern France where most wheat, barley and sugar is grown.
Some light rain was expected over the weekend in the southwestern maize belt.

A dry spell combined with mild temperatures has raised fears of drought among farmers, pushed the government to impose partial irrigation bans in some places and helped to boost the price of French grain on domestic markets.

France's bread basket of Beauce has received only 90 millimetres of rain this year, half the normal level. In the southwest near Bordeaux, 80 millimetres of rain has fallen, only 30 percent of the usual amount.
France's largest farm union, the FNSEA, on Thursday set up a crisis team to monitor crop conditions.
But weather forecasters, government officials and farming experts, while worried by the lack of rain, said they were refusing to forecast a full-blown drought just yet.
"Last year we had the same exact set of circumstances at the same time," said Benedicte Cailler, spokeswoman at the AGPB wheat growers' association.
"Then the situation reversed itself and we had a good harvest."

"It's not a catastrophe," one farmer in the Beauce region told French newspaper Le Monde. "The surface of the fields is dry because of the wind. Underneath it's still wet, but it's time for it to rain."
Analysts said the gradual decline of France's underground water resources was potentially more serious.
